subject: Biotechnology
title: Codeine and CYP2D6
description: A short lesson to help you apply Codeine and CYP2D6.

hook.text: Codeine is a prodrug — it only works after CYP2D6 converts it to morphine. Some people convert too much.

buildup.text: Poor metabolizers get zero pain relief — ultra-rapid metabolizers produce dangerously high morphine levels.

discovery.text: Infant deaths occurred when breastfeeding mothers who were ultra-rapid metabolizers took codeine — morphine in the milk.

twist.text: The FDA now warns against codeine in children under 12 and nursing mothers — pharmacogenomics drove the policy change.

climax.text: CPIC guidelines recommend alternative analgesics for poor and ultra-rapid CYP2D6 metabolizers — test before prescribing.

punchline.text: Same drug, wildly different effects — your CYP2D6 genotype decides what codeine does.

quiz.question: Why is codeine dangerous for CYP2D6 ultra-rapid metabolizers?
options: They break down codeine before it can work, getting no pain relief
They convert codeine to morphine too quickly, reaching dangerous blood levels
They are allergic to all opioid medications
